thread:
Anita (Product): Quick design review request — attaching the latest Figma for the Usage & Billing dashboard. High-level ask: make spend + token breakdown intuitive for orgs with many projects, and make invoices/export easy for finance teams. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz

Sofia (Design): Got it. Two layout proposals in the file: 
- Option A: single page with stacked panels (Spend over time, Token breakdown by model, Top spenders table, Invoices drawer)
- Option B: tabbed view (Overview / Projects / Invoices) with a persistent org selector
I prefer B for discoverability but A feels faster for quick scans.

Mike (Eng): FYI from infra side: the token breakdown per model is expensive to compute on the fly for long time ranges. We have pre-aggregates per-day per-project, and per-model cost is derived from those with a join. We can do near-real-time for last 7d, but anything beyond 30d will need nightly rollups or we point to cached view. Not a blocker, just an engineering tradeoff.

Rahul (Finance): Important: invoices must include proration lines (start/end dates), VAT line items, and a CSV export with per-line token counts. Also customers expect an easy way to download historical invoices. If we hide invoices in a drawer it might be too hidden.

Sofia (Design): Good catch. For accessibility, let's avoid the stacked small sparkline + color-only legend combination. Need: clear labels, >=4.5:1 contrast for text, and a pattern or icon option for token types in charts. I'll update mocks to use dot/hatch patterns and explicit legends.

Lisa (DevEx): Copy nits: the org/project toggle should say "Viewing: Organization / Project" rather than "Org view". And the tooltip for "Token breakdown" should briefly explain "Model tokens billed = prompt tokens + completion tokens + padding" and link to docs.

Anita (Product): Punted decisions: 
1) Use tabbed (Overview / Projects / Invoices) — majority vote.
2) Overview should show 30d spend (default), with quick buttons for 7/30/90. 30d uses cached aggregates, 7d uses near-real-time.
3) Token breakdown: show top 5 models by spend, then an expandable per-project matrix.
4) Invoices: dedicated tab with download/CSV export and invoice viewer.

Mike (Eng): Implementation notes:
- Backend: expose endpoints: `/billing/aggregates?range=30d&group=org` and `/billing/models?range=7d&project_id=xxx`.
- We should add a 'data-staleness' indicator on the UI when showing cached 30d data.

billing-bot: New metric: cost-query-latency spike at 2024-06-07T10:05Z — 95th percentile 2.4s for `/billing/models` (tagged by project). See infra dashboard: https://grafana.company/cost-queries

Mike (Eng): I'll add a debounce + prefetch for the project selector; also add a server-side limit to default to top 10 projects unless "Show all" is clicked.

Rahul (Finance): Also need an API for `GET /invoices?org_id=xxx&start=YYYY-MM-DD&end=YYYY-MM-DD&format=csv` — our accounting team will automate pulls.

Sofia (Design): Accessibility question: when the per-project matrix gets dense, we should allow a data table fallback for screen readers. I'll design a collapsible table view with ARIA labels.

Lisa (DevEx): Small UX copy: the export button should say "Download invoice (CSV)" and open a small modal to choose date range. For newly created invoices show a toast: "Invoice ready — click to download" :tada:

Anita (Product): Next steps: Sofia will push updated mocks by EOD with patterns/contrast fixes and tab layout. Mike will scope the endpoints + an estimate (ETA for a first pass?)

Mike (Eng): I'll post an estimate tomorrow morning. Tentative: 2 sprint slices for Overview + token breakdown (backend + UI), 1 sprint for Invoices viewer + exports depending on auth work.

Rahul (Finance): I'll compile a one-pager with required invoice fields and sample CSV schema and drop here.

Sofia (Design): Pushed updated frames — changed color scheme, added patterns, keyboard nav flows, and a11y notes in figma comments. :eye:

Anita (Product): Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after Mike posts estimates. Quick poll: prefer tabs or stacked? React with :one: for tabs, :two: for stacked.

Mike (Eng): :one:
Sofia (Design): :one:
Rahul (Finance): :one:
Lisa (DevEx): :one:

Anita (Product): Looks like tabs it is. I'll create a ticket to track follow-ups and link mocks + API spec. Closing thread for now — ping here if anything urgent.
